planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Praecox' begins flowering two to three weeks ahead of typical panicle hydrangea cultivars.

directions: Praecox is a historic cultivar of panicle hydrangea selected for flowering two to three weeks ahead of the typical species, opening its creamy white conical flower heads in early to midsummer rather than late summer. Its flower clusters are looser and more open than modern double-flowered selections, showing a higher proportion of small, fertile florets mixed among the larger sterile ones for a lacier, more informal texture. Like other panicle hydrangeas it blooms on new wood, so hard pruning in late winter each year keeps the shrub vigorous and encourages the earliest possible bloom. Its early start extends the panicle hydrangea season in the garden, pairing well with early-summer perennials before later cultivars take over.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Floribunda' bears fuller flower panicles than the wild species without the extreme density of 'Grandiflora'.

directions: Floribunda is an old European selection of panicle hydrangea noted for producing a higher ratio of showy sterile florets than the wild species, giving fuller, more substantial flower panicles without the extreme density of 'Grandiflora'. The cone-shaped flower clusters open white in midsummer and take on soft pink tones as they mature into autumn, held on a rounded, multi-stemmed shrub of moderate size. It flowers reliably on new wood, so an annual late-winter pruning to a framework of strong stems produces the largest and longest-lasting panicles. Its looser, slightly airier flower form makes it a good choice for gardeners wanting a traditional panicle hydrangea look without the heaviness of the most double modern cultivars.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Dharuma' is a true dwarf selection, needing far less room than typical panicle hydrangea cultivars.

directions: Dharuma is a dwarf Japanese selection of panicle hydrangea, growing to only a fraction of the size of the species while retaining proportionally smaller versions of its typical cone-shaped white flower clusters. Its compact, dense habit makes it useful in foundation plantings, mixed borders, and large containers where a full-size panicle hydrangea would quickly outgrow the space. Flowers open white in mid- to late summer and age to soft pink, appearing on new wood, so light pruning in late winter maintains its tidy shape without sacrificing bloom. Because of its small stature, it needs less staking and support than larger panicle hydrangea cultivars, even after heavy rain.

common_name: Webb's Choice Oakleaf Hydrangea (Large-Leaf Native Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; allow ample room, since 'Webb's Choice' is one of the larger-leaved oakleaf hydrangea selections.

directions: Webb's Choice is a Southeastern native selection of oakleaf hydrangea prized for unusually large, deeply lobed leaves and long, dense flower panicles that are proportionally oversized compared with many common oakleaf cultivars. Flowers open white in early summer and age to a rosy pink, held above coarse-textured foliage that turns shades of burgundy and bronze-red in fall. Like other oakleaf hydrangeas it blooms on old wood, so pruning should be limited to right after flowering to avoid removing next year's buds. Its bold scale and vigorous growth suit it best to a woodland-edge or shaded border setting with ample room to reach full size.
